facts.label: Passado simples e present perfect
facts.sub: Passado simples para um momento terminado: I saw it this morning. Present perfect para notícia recente: I’ve just read it, I haven’t read it yet.

facts.label: Passado simples (o que aconteceu)
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para uma notícia com hora ou dia certo: I saw it at breakfast. The storm closed the bridge. Depois do did, o verbo volta ao básico: Did you see it? Did anyone get hurt?

facts.label: Have + particípio (notícia recente)
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para notícia recente, sem hora certa: I’ve just read it. The police have already told people. Particípios úteis: seen, heard, read, gone, written.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “você viu as notícias?” e “já li o artigo”.
compare.us: Em inglês, o passado simples fala de um momento terminado (I saw it at breakfast) e o present perfect, de uma notícia recente (I’ve just read it).

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use the past simple for a finished time, like this morning at nine.
items.why: Yes: I saw it at breakfast.

items.s: We use have + participle for news that is recent and still important.
items.why: Yes: The police have already told people.

items.s: We say “I have saw the news.”
items.why: We say I have seen the news.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use the past simple for a finished time, like this morning at nine. → Verdadeiro (Yes: I saw it at breakfast.)
We use have + participle for news that is recent and still important. → Verdadeiro (Yes: The police have already told people.)
We say “I have saw the news.” → Falso (We say I have seen the news.)

pages.title: A living room in Boston · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy morning in Boston. Noah is at his friend Anya’s home. The radio says a storm hit the coast. Anya has just read a headline on her phone. They have not heard the whole story yet. Noah wants to share what he saw.
“Did you see the news this morning? A big storm hit the coast.” says Anya. “Yes, I saw it at breakfast. Have you heard about the bridge?” says Noah. “No, I haven’t. What happened?” says Anya.
